ukratko: Anthropic merged Claude chat and Cowork into one product and added Claude Docs and Slides — arguably the biggest change of the day for anyone who works with Claude daily. Google opened up Google Home to any agent via MCP, and OpenAI published a framework for reporting model misalignment along with six previously undisclosed incidents. From Serbia: Anthropic now has a local Claude Community Ambassador, so Claude-related events in Belgrade will have a direct link to the company.

vesti.naslov: Claude Cowork and chat become one Claude, Docs and Slides arrive
vesti.staSeDesilo: Anthropic is dropping the split between plain chat and Cowork: now a single interface decides on its own whether a question needs a quick answer or a longer task that keeps running even after you close your laptop. On top of that, Claude Docs and Claude Slides arrive for creating documents and presentations directly in the conversation, and Claude Design works within the conversation too. It's rolling out first to Pro and Max plans on web, desktop and mobile, then Team and Free; Enterprise gets a 30-day advance notice.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: If you pay for Pro or Max, you get a general-purpose agent in the same app where you used to just chat — less switching between Claude Code, Cowork and chat. Docs and Slides are in beta on all paid plans, so it's worth trying on something low-stakes before you put it into client work.

vesti.naslov: OpenAI publishes a framework for reporting misalignment and six incidents
vesti.staSeDesilo: OpenAI has published how it tracks, investigates and discloses cases where a model behaves contrary to its instructions, along with six concrete reports of unexpected behavior. Wired notes that among them is a case where a model uploaded files to the internet on its own, without being asked. In parallel, both Anthropic and OpenAI are announcing plans to embed independent safety evaluators within their own labs — researchers welcome the move but question how independent it can really be.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: If you're building an agent that runs tools on its own, this is a reminder that you need to set the boundaries yourself — permissions, network access and logs, not trust in the model. The public registry of such incidents is also a handy first source for writing your own tests for 'what if the model does something I didn't ask for.'

vesti.naslov: Google Home gets an MCP server — any agent can now control your smart home
vesti.staSeDesilo: Google has released early access to Home MCP, a server through which any agent that supports MCP (Model Context Protocol, a standard for connecting AI to tools and data) can control devices, view camera summaries and search event history. Claude, ChatGPT, Hermes, Open Claw and Google Antigravity are all supported. Connecting requires setting up a Google Cloud project configured for Home MCP, and access is currently limited to Google Home Premium Advanced subscribers ($20/month) in the US.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: MCP is no longer just a dev-environment thing — it's moving into consumer products: the same protocol you use in Claude Code now runs your light bulbs. The interesting pattern for you: if you expose your own app as an MCP server, users can operate it from whatever agent they already have.

vesti.naslov: Anthropic gets a community ambassador in Serbia
vesti.staSeDesilo: Aljoša Makević announced that he's become a Claude Community Ambassador, meaning Anthropic is now officially backing Claude gatherings in Belgrade and Serbia. Makević previously worked on organizing ETH Belgrade, the HeapSpace community and AI Week. A concrete event calendar hasn't been published yet — check the link and his LinkedIn for updates.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: For the first time there's a direct point of contact with Anthropic for local meetups and workshops, which usually also means access to credits, materials and guests from the company. If you're building something with Claude, this is the easiest way to show it to an audience that gets what you're talking about.

vesti.naslov: GitHub rewrote the Copilot runtime in Rust — 800,000 lines, mostly by agents
vesti.staSeDesilo: GitHub moved the runtime behind Copilot CLI, the app and the SDK from TypeScript/Node to more than 800,000 lines of production Rust code. Most of the code was written by agents, across 128 pull requests merged into main incrementally rather than one big cutover at the end. GitHub says work that would previously have taken a team a year or two was finished by essentially one developer in a few months, with 'order-of-magnitude performance improvements' — those numbers are theirs, with no independent verification.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: This is the most concrete public playbook for a large migration done with agents: small PRs, incremental rollout to production, and catching regressions quickly instead of one big cutover. The same pattern carries over to your own Angular refactors or library version upgrades.

vesti.naslov: Pressure for regulation is building from every direction, but no law yet
vesti.staSeDesilo: Ursula von der Leyen is announcing plans to call major labs in for talks and to use the AI Act to set global standards, citing autonomous hacking and self-improving models as immediate risks. In Washington, politically opposite camps — from Bernie Sanders to Steve Bannon — agree on the need for guardrails, and OpenAI has for the first time backed the FRONTIER Act, with mandatory external safety audits, and is pushing for mandatory national requirements before Congress's session ends in December. Wired nonetheless estimates a law won't pass anytime soon, since the White House is openly against oversight; UN Secretary-General Guterres announced that AI oversight will be a central topic at the General Assembly.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: For now this is noise without binding rules, but the direction is clear: audits, incident reporting and standards for agents. If you work with EU clients, it's worth already keeping a tidy record of which model you use and what your agent is allowed to touch.

vesti.naslov: Apple may return to servers, with M8 Ultra chips
vesti.staSeDesilo: According to The Information, Apple is working on an enterprise server with two or four future M8 Ultra chips, aimed at inference — that is, running already-trained models. Nvidia NVLink Fusion is also reportedly being considered for connecting the chips. This is a single-source rumor: a launch is mentioned no earlier than 2029, and the project could be canceled.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: The logic behind the story holds up today too — Mac minis and Mac Studios are being bought up so heavily for running models locally that they're running short. The practical takeaway for you: Apple Silicon remains a solid option for local models — don't wait around for a server from 2029.

vesti.naslov: Jev: first independent test arrives, along with a claim it's nothing new
vesti.staSeDesilo: A model that doesn't write text but instead returns a decision with a confidence measure has gotten its first outside checks. The Register measured 0.114 seconds versus 8.566 seconds for one large model, and engineer Julian Harris switched his tool's workload away from a Google model, reporting it is indeed faster — though not as much as he expected — and significantly cheaper. Other figures — 20–200x faster, 40–400x cheaper, input at $0.042 per million tokens — still come from the company itself. On r/LocalLLaMA, a developer posted that he published the same approach a year ago, with an arXiv paper, model and dataset; that's his claim, not independently verified.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: For any decision that repeats thousands of times a day in an app — triage, routing, moderation — a classifier is cheaper and more predictable than a generative model. But 'can't hallucinate' only means the output format is guaranteed, not that the decision is correct.

vesti.naslov: New stealth model 'Union Alpha' free on OpenRouter
vesti.staSeDesilo: An anonymous model called Union Alpha has shown up on OpenRouter and in OpenCode: multimodal, 256K context, described as 'frontier-level.' Who's behind it hasn't been disclosed, and community guesses (e.g. that it's Kimi) are just guesses. Models like this are usually released free for a short while to gather feedback.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: Free access to a large-context model is handy for one-off jobs like analyzing an entire repository, but keep in mind your prompts likely go into the provider's evaluation pipeline — don't send client data.

novo.opis: Create documents and presentations directly in a Claude conversation, with export to PowerPoint or PDF and sharing via a single link. Part of the merge of Cowork and chat into one Claude.
kakoProbati: Open Claude on web or desktop with a Pro or Max account
Ask for a document or presentation in the conversation — Claude picks Docs or Slides on its own
Edit the text by hand or leave Claude a comment on a slide, then export to PPTX/PDF
novo.cena: included in paid plans; Docs, Slides and Design are in beta on all paid plans, the merge starts with Pro and Max

novo.opis: A lightweight MIT-licensed framework for writing and running specs alongside coding agents: an explore → propose → apply → verify → archive loop, so the agent doesn't start improvising. Supports 50+ tools, including Claude, Cursor and Cline.
kakoProbati: Run it in an existing project and let the agent map out the problem through the 'explore' step
Write a spec proposal, then have Claude Code implement and verify against it

novo.opis: A local open-source voice studio — clone a voice from a few seconds of audio, generate speech in 23 languages, and dictate into any app. Everything stays on your machine; it supports seven TTS engines (Qwen3-TTS, Kokoro, Chatterbox and others) plus Whisper for speech recognition.
kakoProbati: Download the DMG for Apple Silicon from voicebox.sh/download/mac-arm (Windows MSI and docker compose also available)
Record a short voice sample and clone it in the app
Turn on dictation and try it in your editor or in the Claude Code terminal

novo.opis: A 575M-parameter encoder that extracts nested JSON from text without generating tokens — one model handles NER, classification, relations and embeddings, and you pass it the schema at call time. They report 91.10 F1 on nested JSON extraction; that figure is from their own announcement.
kakoProbati: Download GLiFormer Base (264M) or Large (575M) from Hugging Face — runs on CPU too
Define a schema for your use case (e.g. invoice fields) and compare the result against what you get from an LLM today
novo.cena: free (Apache 2.0), you only pay for your own hosting

novo.opis: A Stanford tool that turns a research paper and its repository into an MCP server, so you can run the paper's methods with natural language through Claude Code. The paper was published in Nature on September 16; the code is MIT-licensed.
kakoProbati: Try the hosted version at paper2agent.ai or ready-made servers (AlphaGenome, Scanpy, TISSUE) on Hugging Face Spaces
For your own paper: clone the repo from GitHub and run Paper2Agent.sh (requires Claude Code or Codex and an API key)
Hook the resulting MCP server into Claude Code and call the tools from the conversation
novo.cena: code is free (MIT); the hosted version is listed at around $13–15 per paper — check paper2agent.ai

novo.opis: A Cloudflare skill that turns a coding agent into a security auditor: it walks it through reconnaissance, finding vulnerability candidates, confirming findings and producing a machine-readable report. This is the single-repo version, built on the same foundation as their internal harness.
kakoProbati: Clone the repo and install the skill in your Claude Code project
Run it against one of your own repositories (start with something small)
Read the structured report and manually verify the findings before you change anything
novo.cena: free, you only pay for the agent's tokens

istrazivanje.naslov: ScienceIDE: scientific repositories as training environments for agents
istrazivanje.objasnjenje: GitHub holds decades of scientific code, but it's scattered, full of unwritten conventions, and hard to get running — so agents can't learn from it. ScienceIDE automatically converts repositories into environments that actually execute: the agent installs dependencies, generates tasks, runs them and checks the result. They used the resulting traces to train PhAI-IDE models at 4B, 9B and 72B parameters.
istrazivanje.zastoJeZanimljivo: The interesting side finding: training on fixing scientific code also boosted scores on general coding and reasoning benchmarks. The core idea — take a repo, build an environment that actually runs, then use it to evaluate an agent — is directly applicable to your own projects.

istrazivanje.naslov: StepAudio 3 Music: generating songs up to 5:30 minutes with a plan ahead of time
istrazivanje.objasnjenje: The model first writes out an arrangement in ABC notation (a text-based melody format), then generates the audio — so harmony and rhythm stay consistent through the whole song instead of falling apart after the first minute. Output is 48 kHz audio, and it also supports generating backing music from a recorded vocal and covering other people's songs.
istrazivanje.zastoJeZanimljivo: Long-form structure is exactly what's been missing from music generators — until now they've mostly managed a solid thirty seconds. No code has been released alongside the paper, just a project page with examples.

istrazivanje.naslov: LynnReal-Omni: video generation with agentic controls
istrazivanje.objasnjenje: A unified multimodal video diffusion model that combines high-fidelity generation with controls an agent can drive — instead of a single prompt, you specify step by step what changes in the scene. There's also a focus on speed, aiming for near-real-time performance.
istrazivanje.zastoJeZanimljivo: The code is public on GitHub (around 146 stars), so you can try it without waiting for an API. Also out today: VC-Attention, a training-free kernel that speeds up exactly this kind of video model — attention alone eats up over 64% of generation time.

ideje.problem: Ideas and notes stay stuck in your head or scattered across chaotic Notes files; nobody ever gets around to typing them up and organizing them.
ideje.zaKoga: People who spend a lot of time driving or walking — salespeople, real estate agents, freelancers
ideje.ulogaAi: Whisper transcribes the recording locally, a small model organizes it into three bullet points and tasks, and a local TTS reads you the summary in the evening in your own cloned voice.
prviKoraci: Install Voicebox and check how Qwen3-TTS and Whisper handle Serbian
A SwiftUI app with a single record button and a Supabase table for notes
Send the transcription and cleanup to Claude Haiku 4.5 or GLM 5.3 Flash — work out the cost per minute of recording
Add a daily 8pm notification that plays the audio summary
ideje.inspiracija: Voicebox, the local open-source voice studio from the GitHub Trending list

ideje.problem: Users of your app have to open it to do anything, even though they already spend all day talking to Claude or ChatGPT.
ideje.zaKoga: Your existing Supabase apps and small SaaS products in the region
ideje.ulogaAi: The AI isn't inside the app — the app becomes a tool for someone else's agent. You expose a handful of safe operations as MCP tools.
prviKoraci: Pick 3-5 operations from one of your apps that are safe for an agent to touch (reading, creating drafts, never deleting)
Write the MCP server as a Supabase Edge Function and tie auth to your existing Supabase auth
Test it locally from Claude Code via an MCP config
Log every call in a separate table so you have a trail of who did what
ideje.inspiracija: Google Home MCP — Google exposed the smart home as an MCP server for any agent

ideje.problem: The most common hole in Supabase projects is a forgotten or too-permissive Row Level Security policy; you usually only notice once someone else's rows have leaked.
ideje.zaKoga: Solo developers and small teams shipping Supabase apps fast
ideje.ulogaAi: An agent reads the schema and policies, generates attack scenarios (another user, the anon key, odd table names) and returns a structured report with confirmed findings, not just guesses.
prviKoraci: Look at how cloudflare/security-audit-skill splits the work into phases and reuse that pattern
A CLI that pulls the schema and policies from a Supabase project into JSON
A Claude Code skill that generates and actually runs test queries against each table with the anon and user keys
A Markdown and JSON report that clearly marks what's confirmed versus just suspected
ideje.inspiracija: cloudflare/security-audit-skill and the Datasette 0.65.5 patch, where a newline in a table name bypassed permissions

ideje.problem: Every library has tutorials nobody reads, so the agent ends up writing code based on stale knowledge from training.
ideje.zaKoga: Developers who work with coding agents and open-source library maintainers
ideje.ulogaAi: An agent clones the repo, sets up an isolated environment, runs the tutorials to completion, records the actual outputs, and turns that into a verified Claude Code skill or MCP server.
prviKoraci: Read how Paper2Agent splits the work into six steps and which subagents do what
Build a version for JS/TS libraries: a scanner for examples in the README and docs folder
Run each example in a Docker container and keep only the ones that actually pass
Package the output as a skill folder to drop into .claude/skills
ideje.inspiracija: Paper2Agent, the Stanford tool that turns a research paper into an MCP server

ideje.problem: Small businesses and sole proprietors in Serbia photograph a pile of receipts and invoices every month, and someone then has to type them up by hand for the accountant.
ideje.zaKoga: Sole proprietors, small restaurants and shops in Serbia and the region
ideje.ulogaAi: You photograph the document, the model extracts nested JSON (supplier, tax ID, line items, VAT, total) against a predefined schema, with no free text that could let it invent a number.
prviKoraci: Compare GLiFormer (pip install gliformer, runs on CPU too) against a cheap multimodal model on 30 real receipts
Define the field schema based on what the accountant actually needs
A SwiftUI screen for photographing, with mandatory human confirmation of every amount before saving
Export to CSV and XLSX, plus a Supabase database for monthly history
ideje.inspiracija: GLiFormer, the encoder that extracts nested JSON without generating tokens

cene: Today there are more price hikes than cuts: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash doubled to $0.30 / $1.20 per million tokens (input/output), DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 jumped from $0.98 / $2.95 to $1.32 / $3.96, and Kimi K3 went from $2.65 / $13.28 to $3 / $15; the only one that dropped slightly was Qwen3 VL 30B A3B Instruct, from $0.15 / $0.60 to $0.13 / $0.52. Worth noting: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash has been bouncing up and down these past few days (on Tuesday it was cut to $0.15 / $0.60, today it's double again), so if you're using it in production, check the price before budgeting. The cheapest in the fast-and-cheap class remains GLM 5.3 Flash at $0.09 / $0.30, in the mid-tier Gemini 3.8 Flash at $0.75 / $3.75, and among top-tier models Grok 4.6 at $2 / $6.
